summary: Fresno County lookout on Owens Mountain, named Copper Peak in 1935, closed 1980, burned 1985; listed gone; communications sites occupy the peak now.

facts.design: enclosed tower (per the Fire Lookout Association list)
facts.status_note: Burned down in 1985 per Fresno County Fire; KVPR calls the fire arson. Communications towers and an automated wildfire lookout occupy the peak today.

staffing.status: manned; a lookout worked there until retiring in 1965

events.note: KVPR: the state established a fire lookout at the summit and named it Copper Peak
July 1944 grass fire from the army rifle range near Owens Mountain; the Copper Peak station was first to report it
Division of Forestry photograph of the lookout garage dated November 22, 1957
Perry David Corbly worked at the station before retiring in 1965 (1966 obituary)
KVPR says decommissioned; Fresno County Fire says closed
Fresno County Fire: burned down; KVPR: destroyed in an arson fire

evidence.supports: state established a lookout at the summit in 1935 and named it Copper Peak
evidence.quote: In 1935, the state established a fire lookout at the summit, and named it Copper Peak.

evidence.supports: mountain location north of Clovis and northeast Fresno, about 1,000 feet above the valley floor
evidence.quote: It looms over the northern Clovis and northeast Fresno, rising around 1000 feet above the valley floor.

evidence.supports: closed 1980; destroyed by arson fire in 1985
evidence.quote: The lookout was decommissioned in 1980, and was destroyed in an arson fire in 1985.

evidence.supports: communications towers and an automated lookout occupy the peak today
evidence.quote: Today communications towers and an automated wildfire lookout occupy the peak.

evidence.supports: agency listed as California Department of Forestry
evidence.quote: Fresno County - California Department of Forestry

evidence.supports: July 22, 1944 grass fire started on the army rifle range near Owens Mountain
evidence.quote: July 22, 1944: State division of forestry fire suppression crews fought for nearly five hours yesterday afternoon before bringing under control a grass fire which started on the army rifle range near Owens Mountain

evidence.supports: the blaze swept east over Owens Mountain
evidence.quote: The blaze fanned by a wind, swept east over Owens Mountain and burned a strip approximately a quarter of a mile wide and four miles long.

evidence.supports: March 11, 1966 obituary: retired fire lookout for the State Division of Forestry
evidence.quote: March 11, 1966: Perry David Corbly, 81, a retired fire lookout for the State Division of Forestry, died yesterday in a Fresno hospital after a long illness.

evidence.supports: KVPR: served as an important early warning system for fires in the foothills and the growing Fresno and Clovis area
evidence.quote: It served as an important early warning system for both fires in the foothills and also in the growing urban area of Fresno and Clovis.

evidence.supports: California Division of Forestry records (state source) for the 1957 garage photograph
evidence.quote: The photograph is part of the Black Cards collection of California Division of Forestry records housed at the Cal Fire Museum.

evidence.supports: Copper Peak station first reported the 1944 fire
evidence.quote: which first reported the fire shortly before 3 P.M.

evidence.supports: Perry David Corbly worked at the station before retiring in 1965
evidence.quote: He worked at the Copper Peak fire lookout station in the Fresno Ranger Unit before his retirement in 1965.

evidence.supports: photograph of the lookout garage dated November 22, 1957
evidence.quote: This is a photograph from Fresno County of the garage at Copper Peak lookout on November 22, 1957.

evidence.supports: lookout closed in 1980 and burned down in 1985
evidence.quote: Copper Peak Lookout: Located on Owens Mountain above the east end of rural Clovis and closed in 1980. It burned down in 1985.

evidence.supports: listed in Fresno County as an enclosed tower, now gone
evidence.quote: Copper Peak (Owens Mountain) Fresno 36.92997 -119.64163 Encl. Tower Gone

notes_for_editor: The 1980 closure and 1985 fire agree across KVPR and Fresno County Fire. The 1935 build date comes from KVPR alone; Forest Lookouts gives no build date. The Fresno County Fire line about a station opened in the early 1930s refers to McKenzie Fire Camp, not this lookout, and was not used. The Internet Archive Black Cards items are public domain per their rights notes, but no direct image URL was verified, so no photos were added. Whether the summit is public is not stated in any source; access key omitted.
